key_insight: TextSeal2 embeds a detectable watermark in LLM-generated text without changing the model’s output distribution. Its watermark survives speculative decoding—even when rejected draft tokens are replaced—without changing the acceptance rate.
problem_solved: Watermarking must remain detectable without sacrificing output diversity or disrupting fast generation. Speculative decoding adds a challenge: replacement tokens must retain the watermark signal.
method: Uses copula mixing and memoryless races as its core watermarking approach, as indicated by the paper’s title.
Keeps replacement tokens watermarked under the same keys when speculative drafts are rejected, while preserving the acceptance rate.
Preserves output diversity and reports no measurable added inference latency. The supplied abstract is truncated, so detailed algorithmic steps are unavailable.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, TextSeal2 offers a way to mark generated text while retaining speculative-decoding speedups and output diversity. The reported lack of measurable inference overhead makes it promising for production serving.
